meta.source: IEEE MA-L/MA-M/MA-S registry (standards-oui.ieee.org) + curated LE attribution, adversarially verified

confidence_meaning.high: Vendor's hardware is near-exclusively LE / first-responder gear; an OUI match is strong evidence.
confidence_meaning.medium: Public-safety-heavy but also broad enterprise/consumer lines; corroborate.
confidence_meaning.low: General-purpose device merely common in cruisers; weak on its own.

ota_emission_meaning.confirmed: Brand OUI is documented to appear over-the-air (Wi-Fi BSSID and/or non-randomized BLE).
ota_emission_meaning.router_bssid: Router assigns its brand OUI to its Wi-Fi BSSID, so it is emitted over-the-air.
ota_emission_meaning.unverified: Unknown whether the device's radio emits the brand OUI OTA (camera radio may present a COTS module OUI).
ota_emission_meaning.wired_only: Brand OUI appears on the wired NIC/dock only; the OTA Wi-Fi/BT MAC is a COTS module OUI.

caveats: An OUI identifies a VENDOR, not a device model, and is never proof of active policing.

MAC randomization: unassociated Wi-Fi probe requests and BLE advertising commonly use locally-administered (randomized) MACs carrying no vendor OUI. Vendor OUIs reliably appear only on factory/public MACs (an associated Wi-Fi client, a router BSSID, or a BT-Classic public address).

OTA-emission reality: except for Axon (00:25:DF, confirmed on Wi-Fi+BLE) and the in-vehicle routers, most body cameras and rugged MDTs emit their COTS radio-MODULE maker's OUI over the air, not the brand OUI — see each vendor's ota_emission and the module_oui_vendors list.

Module-OUI blind spot: Getac, COBAN Technologies (Houston), i-PRO, BK Technologies, Wolfcom, Reveal Media, Edesix, and Pinnacle Response hold NO IEEE block, so they cannot be matched by a brand OUI at all.
Name-collision traps are enumerated in exclusions[].

vendors.name: Axon Enterprise, Inc.
vendors.note: Near-exclusive US law-enforcement vendor: Axon Body 2/3/4 body cameras, Axon Fleet in-car video, TASER CEWs. The ONLY vendor here with public evidence of emitting its own OUI over the air — both the Wi-Fi BSSID and the (non-randomized) BLE advertising MAC start with 00:25:DF. A match means 'an Axon device' (cam/dock/Fleet/TASER), not strictly 'recording'.
vendors.false_positive_notes: Not the defunct 'Axon Networks Inc.' (00:58:28 / 00:C0:D4 / 84:70:03) — see exclusions.

vendors.name: Digital Ally, Inc.
vendors.note: FirstVU Pro/HD body cameras and DVM-800/EVO-HD in-car video for LE/first responders (VuLink cross-activation). OTA emission of 00:23:BD by the camera radio is unverified — the VuLink Wi-Fi link may present a module OUI.

vendors.name: WatchGuard Video (Motorola Solutions)
vendors.note: 4RE in-car video and V300/VISTA body cameras; acquired by Motorola Solutions (2019). In-car VISTA WiFi Base broadcasts a recording-group AP. Anchor on OUI 00:1D:96 or Motorola Solutions OUIs, not on any SSID string.
vendors.false_positive_notes: Distinct from WatchGuard Technologies (firewalls, 00:01:21 / 00:90:7F) — see exclusions.

vendors.name: L-3 Communications Mobile-Vision, Inc.
vendors.note: Flashback in-car video DVRs for police fleets (now a Safe Fleet LE brand). DVR uploads via the station AP at shift change (client mode); passive-detect via probe/association using OUI 38:73:EA:0.

vendors.name: VIEVU
vendors.note: Police body cameras (LE-3/4/5). Acquired by Axon (2018), line discontinued but units remain fielded — a match is legacy but police-specific.

vendors.name: Motorola Solutions Inc.
vendors.note: Public-safety LMR (APX/MOTOTRBO), dispatch, and body/in-car video via WatchGuard. NOT Motorola Mobility (Lenovo phones, excluded).
vendors.false_positive_notes: Do not confuse with 'Motorola Mobility LLC, a Lenovo Company'.

vendors.name: Harris Corporation (L3Harris)
vendors.note: L3Harris public-safety P25 LMR (XL/XG series). Also broadcast/other RF.

vendors.name: Sepura Limited
vendors.note: TETRA / public-safety subscriber radios; predominant among EU/UK police.

vendors.name: Tait Communications (Tait Electronics)
vendors.note: Public-safety LMR (P25/DMR/TETRA).
vendors.false_positive_notes: Distinct from 'TAIT Global LLC' (8C:1F:64:A7:8), entertainment staging — see exclusions.

vendors.name: E.F. Johnson (EFJohnson Technologies)
vendors.note: Dedicated US public-safety P25 vendor (Viking VP-series; ATLAS P25 systems). CAVEAT: VP Bluetooth is usually a third-party multi-pin adapter, so the on-air BT MAC is the adapter maker's, not 00:08:B8.

vendors.name: JVCKENWOOD Corporation (Kenwood)
vendors.note: NX-5000 multi-protocol (P25/NXDN/DMR) portables used by some agencies, but Kenwood LMR is commercial-dominant — weak police signal on its own.

vendors.name: Hytera Communications Corp. Ltd.
vendors.note: DMR portables, some TETRA. Commercial/security-dominant; US LE adoption sharply limited by NDAA Sec.889. Higher (medium) relevance in some non-US jurisdictions.

vendors.name: Airbus Defence and Space (TETRA, ex-Cassidian/EADS)
vendors.note: TETRA handsets (TH1n/THR9/THR9i) common on European police TETRA networks. Corporate blocks are broad, not TETRA-specific.

ouis.org: Airbus Defence and Space Deutschland GmbH

vendors.name: Codan Radio Communications
vendors.note: P25 LMR infrastructure + HF radio; more infrastructure/HF than Wi-Fi/BLE-emitting handhelds — low passive relevance.

ouis.org: Daniels Electronics Ltd. dba Codan Radio Communications

vendors.name: Simoco (Team Simoco)
vendors.note: DMR/analog LMR; utilities/transport/some international public safety; limited US presence.

vendors.name: Thales Communications Inc.
vendors.note: Liberty multiband SDR P25 portable (niche) + broad tactical/military line. Other Thales divisions' OUIs are unrelated — do not attribute.

vendors.name: Icom Inc.
vendors.note: IC-F IDAS/NXDN and select P25 LMR; predominantly commercial/amateur, limited US police P25 footprint. BT only via optional module.

vendors.name: Selex Communications (Leonardo)
vendors.note: Niche professional/TETRA radio, primarily European. Broad 'Leonardo' blocks are not radio-specific — do not attribute those.

vendors.name: Vertex Standard LMR, Inc.
vendors.note: Commercial/business LMR, NOT front-line P25 public safety. Low police relevance.

vendors.name: Cradlepoint, Inc.
vendors.note: Cellular routers very widely deployed in police cruisers (COR/IBR/R-series); the router assigns its OUI to its Wi-Fi BSSID (emitted on-air). Also broad enterprise/IoT use — medium.

vendors.name: Sierra Wireless, ULC
vendors.note: AirLink MG90/MP70 are FirstNet public-safety in-vehicle routers with documented LE use (offloading V300 BWC / 4RE video). Capped at medium: identical AirLink hardware is heavily deployed in transit/rail/utilities and Sierra modules ride inside countless third-party devices.

vendors.name: Peplink / Pepwave
vendors.note: Mobile/failover routers used in some public-safety vehicles; broadly general-purpose (RV/marine/transit/SMB) — weak on its own.

vendors.name: Utility, Inc. (BodyWorn)
vendors.note: In-vehicle 'Rocket IoT' router/MDT connectivity for LE. ATTRIBUTION CAVEAT: verifiers agreed IEEE lists 'Utility, Inc' but could not fully rule out a same-name company. The BodyWorn camera runs on a ruggedized-Android phone, so its Wi-Fi/BLE MAC is the phone SoC's, NOT these OUIs — treat these prefixes as fleet/MDT (Rocket), not BWC.
vendors.false_positive_notes: Not 'Vutility Inc' (D4:63:52, energy metering) — see exclusions.

vendors.name: Panasonic Connect Co., Ltd.
vendors.note: Toughbook rugged MDTs used by police. Toughbook Wi-Fi/BT is a COTS Intel module (e.g. AX201), so these Panasonic OUIs appear on the WIRED NIC/dock, not over the air. NOTE: the Arbitrator in-car video line was spun off to i-PRO in 2019 (see module-OUI vendors), so in_car_video is NOT attributed here.

vendors.name: Seon Design Inc. (Safe Fleet)
vendors.note: Primarily transit/school-bus mobile DVR/NVR (Trooper/Explorer HD/vMax). Useful mainly as the citable Safe-Fleet-family OUI proxy, since Safe Fleet's LE brand COBAN has no OUI of its own. Weight low for LE patrol.

vendors.name: Rosco, Inc. (Rosco Vision Systems)
vendors.note: Fleet/commercial/school-bus DVRs (Dual-Vision/DV6/RoscoLive) — low LE-patrol relevance.

vendors.name: Kymeta
vendors.note: Flat-panel electronically-steered SATCOM on some gov/first-responder vehicles; primarily gov/mil/maritime.

vendors.name: Zepcam B.V.
vendors.note: Body-worn cameras for police/security/first-responders (primarily EU). Also private-security use, hence medium. OTA brand-OUI emission unverified.

vendors.name: Digital Barriers
vendors.note: Body-worn and covert surveillance / live streaming (EdgeVis). Used by police, military and security.

vendors.name: Federal Signal SSG
vendors.note: Emergency-vehicle light bars/sirens/warning. Rarely Wi-Fi/BLE-emitting — low passive relevance; kept for completeness.

module_oui_vendors.name: Getac (Video Solutions / Technology Corp.)
module_oui_vendors.reason: No IEEE OUI under 'Getac'. BC-0x body cams, VR-X10 in-car DVR, B360/F110 MDTs all ride on COTS radios (Intel AX201 Wi-Fi + Sierra WWAN) — OTA MAC is the module maker's.

module_oui_vendors.name: COBAN Technologies, Inc. (Houston, Safe Fleet)
module_oui_vendors.reason: Genuine LE in-car DVR maker (EDGE/Focus/Titan) with NO IEEE OUI. On-air MAC is the module maker's. Distinct from 'COBAN SRL' (Italy) which is denylisted. Safe-Fleet-family OUI proxy is Seon Design (00:1C:3C).

module_oui_vendors.name: i-PRO Americas Inc. (ex-Panasonic i-PRO)
module_oui_vendors.reason: Owns the Arbitrator 360/360HD in-car DVR + BWC4000 body cam after the 2019 Panasonic spin-off. No OUI attributable to Arbitrator/BWC4000; the 360HD's integrated 802.11n uses an Intel/COTS-module OUI, and installs often pair with a Utility 'Rocket' router that is the real RF emitter.

module_oui_vendors.name: BK Technologies (RELM / Bendix King)
module_oui_vendors.reason: High-value US federal/wildland-fire P25 gear (KNG2 series) with built-in Bluetooth, but NO IEEE OUI — the BLE MAC is a COTS module's (Nordic/TI/Qualcomm) or a random address. Not OUI-detectable.

module_oui_vendors.name: WOLFCOM Enterprises
module_oui_vendors.reason: No IEEE OUI. Rebrands Asian-ODM cameras (Halo/Vision/3rd Eye); Wi-Fi models expose the module chipmaker's OUI.

module_oui_vendors.name: Reveal Media Ltd
module_oui_vendors.reason: No IEEE OUI. D-Series (D5) Wi-Fi/BT live-stream + BLE triggers ride on the COTS module OUI. Do not conflate with Digital Barriers (00:24:39).

module_oui_vendors.name: Edesix Ltd / VideoBadge (Motorola)
module_oui_vendors.reason: No IEEE OUI under 'Edesix'/'VaaS'. VB-300/VB-400 (now Motorola VB400) Wi-Fi models expose the COTS module OUI; a Motorola-provisioned MAC is possible but unverified.

module_oui_vendors.name: Pinnacle Response Ltd
module_oui_vendors.reason: No IEEE OUI. PR6/PR7 are ODM-built by Computime (00:1E:5E); the OTA Wi-Fi OUI is most likely the embedded chip's, and Wi-Fi is off by default (cradle/side-button only).

fingerprints.source: WiGLE / vertex.link crowdsourced; DEF CON 31 RFParty
fingerprints.caveat: Camera streaming/upload SoftAP name (e.g. AXON-X6032638M). Crowdsourced, not an Axon spec; the BSSID OUI 00:25:DF is the more reliable anchor.
Default '<Model>-<3 hex>' SSID (e.g. IBR900-xxx). GENERAL-PURPOSE router, not police-exclusive; fleet units usually rename/hide the SSID via NetCloud.
Community-reported default 'PEPWAVE_XXXX'/'PEPLINK_XXXX'; commonly customized in the field. Broad non-police user base.
